web.how: every route already has its own address; with hosts listed, the web build writes /.well-known/apple-app-site-association when TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID is set and /.well-known/assetlinks.json when tac.origin and TAC_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256 are set, and prints a note for each one it cannot write

macos.note: tac.application.links: the macOS app claims the listed schemes in Info.plist and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. Links to the listed hosts stay in the browser, because the unsigned app has no associated domains (PKG1).

windows.note: tac.application.links: the Windows app registers the listed schemes for the current user when it starts (a --release MSIX package declares them as windows.protocol extensions instead), and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A link that arrives while the app runs goes to the open window. Links to the listed hosts stay in the browser, because the app declares no app URI handlers.

linux.note: tac.application.links: the Linux .desktop file claims the listed schemes once it is installed, as the release .deb and AppImage do, and the app opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A link that arrives while the app runs goes to the open window. Linux has no verified web links, so links to the listed hosts stay in the browser.

ios.note: tac.application.links: the iOS app claims the listed schemes in Info.plist and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. Universal links to the listed hosts need TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID and a --device or --release build, whose profile has the Associated Domains capability; no signed build has opened one on a device yet. A simulator build opens only the custom schemes.

android.note: tac.application.links: the Android app claims the listed schemes, and https links to the listed hosts with autoVerify, and opens them at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. Android verifies the hosts only when each one serves /.well-known/assetlinks.json with the app's signing certificate (TAC_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256); until then it asks which app opens their links.

macos.note: ty bundle --release builds a .dmg whose app is signed with the team's Developer ID certificate and the hardened runtime, then notarizes and staples it; the team and notary profile come from TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID and TAC_APPLE_NOTARY_PROFILE. No release has been notarized on a Mac yet. Other builds are an ad hoc signed .app.

windows.how: ty bundle --target windows --release builds an MSIX package, <Name>.msix, with makeappx and signs it with signtool and the certificate that TAC_WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE (a .pfx file) or TAC_WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_THUMBPRINT (a certificate in the store) names; TAC_WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PUBLISHER is the package publisher. Other builds are a folder with the .exe

linux.how: ty bundle --release builds an AppImage and a .deb that install the app, its command, desktop file, AppStream metainfo and icons; both use the system's GTK 4 and WebKitGTK 6. Other builds are a folder

ios.note: ty bundle --release builds an .ipa for App Store Connect, signed with the App Store profile that TAC_IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE names and its keychain certificate, and --device builds one for a registered iPhone or iPad; the team comes from TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID. A --device build was signed and checked on a Mac; --release, an install on a device and an upload have not run yet. Other builds run in the simulator.

android.how: ty bundle --release builds an APK and an AAB signed with the keystore that TAC_ANDROID_KEYSTORE names; other builds are a debug APK

macos.note: The macOS build passes SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and ZERO_AR_DATE to swiftc and compiles from the source folder, so two builds should match. A repeat-build run on a Mac is still owed (TL2). A --release .dmg differs between builds: its secure timestamp and notarization ticket change.

windows.note: The Windows build compiles and links with /Brepro and keeps .obj files out of the output, so two builds should match. A repeat-build run on Windows is still owed (TL2).

linux.how: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and a path map reach cc and rustc, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH reaches dpkg-deb and mksquashfs; two packaged builds give the same artifact-manifest.json digests

ios.note: The iOS build passes SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and ZERO_AR_DATE to swiftc and compiles from the source folder, so two builds should match. A repeat-build run on a Mac is still owed (TL2).

android.note: The Android build turns on Gradle's reproducible archives and drops Gradle's build folders from the output. The debug APK is signed with the build machine's debug key, so it matches only on the same machine. A repeat-build run is still owed (TL2).
